claims.head: A shadow job for Miller, Dorofeyev and Kartye
claims.call: The Rangers’ L2 (Miller, Dorofeyev and Kartye) spends at least 42% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Dorofeyev’s line (Miller, Dorofeyev and Kartye) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would. That’s a checking assignment: Mike Sullivan wants this group on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Pettersson and Lekkerimäki.
claims.nums: At home: 42% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 29% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Mike Sullivan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canucks’ first line.

NYR.head: The Rangers have nearly everything going for them
NYR.body: The Rangers have controlled the play far better over recent games, Vancouver is playing for the second night in a row, and the Rangers have home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Vancouver can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.

VAN.head: A steep climb for Vancouver
VAN.body: The Rangers have controlled the play far better over recent games, Vancouver is playing for the second night in a row, and the Rangers have home ice. Vancouver’s best hope is pouncing on loose pucks, plus a big night in goal.
